I feel the video was a little disingenuous, or possibly was created by someone who isn't familiar with all the theoretical issues. There are many possible voting systems, but it is well-known in technical circles that no voting system can offer all intuitively desirable characteristics (Arrow's Impossibility Theorem), and that in any practically acceptable voting system there are cases where strategic voting cannot be avoided (Gibbard-Satterthwaite Theorem). Certainly, voting systems can be changed, but there are advantages to the "first past the post" system, as well as disadvantages. In particular, even in cases like the last election, where there was great diversity of opinion, there is still a high probability that a winner emerges with a clear majority. This has substantial advantages in terms of governmental stability, and this in turn may well lead to economic stability. Even where coalitions are formed, they tend to be long-lasting. The UK has not faced the kind of governmental instability that (for example) Belgium and Italy have had to deal with for many decades.

As for the possibility of changing the voting system, it's worth noting that the UK held a referendum on replacing "first past the post" with the "alternative vote" just four years ago, and the proposed change, which would have been a clear first step towards changing the electoral system, was decisively rejected.

I should say that I also felt it was a little hypocritical to hear a voice from the other side of the Atlantic commenting adversely on the UK's voting system, when both the USA and Canada use the same "first past the post" voting method.

Listen, I will recount the best of dreams, which came to me in the middle of the night, after speech-bearers turned to rest. It seemed to me that I saw a most wondrous tree, the brightest of rood-trees, raised aloft, encircled by light. That beacon was completely covered with gold; studded with beautiful jewels at its base and with five upon the shoulder-beam, like a sword.

All those made pure through eternal decree, looked upon the Hanged Gods' valkyries there. Nor was it a criminal's tree; but holy spirits, men over the earth, and all this glorious creation of the gods gazed upon it. Wondrous was the tree of victory, whilst I was stained with evil, badly wounded with iniquity. I saw the tree of glory, richly clothed, shining joyfully, adorned with gold. Jewels covered splendidly the Raven-Lord's tree.

But still through that gold I could sense the ancient hostility of the wretched ones, as it had immediately begun to bleed on the right side. I was engulfed in sorrow; fearful because of that beautiful vision. I saw that shining beacon change covering and colour; sometimes it was drenched with blood, soaked with blood's flow, sometimes adorned with treasure.

I lay there a long time gazing at the grey-beard's troubled tree, until I heard it call out. The best wood then began to speak words: "That was years gone by, I still remember, that I was hewn down at the forest's edge, cut out of my tree trunk. Strong foes took me there and made me into a display for themselves, ordered me to hoist up their criminals. Warriors carried me on shoulders, until they set me up on a hill; many foes fastened me there.

Then I saw the All-father hasten with great zeal; he wished to climb on me. I dared not contradict the god's will when I saw the earth’s surface trembling. I could have slayed all the foes, but I stood firm. The young spear-god stripped himself strong and resolute. He stepped up onto the high gallows, brave in the sight of many, where he would set the runes free. I shook when the warrior embraced me. I didn’t dare to bow down to the earth, fall to the ground. I was raised as a Irminsul! I raised Iron Mask aloft, the Lord of the Slain, I dared not bend.

Then they pierced me with dark nails. The wounds were visible on me, open vicious wounds. But I didn’t dare harm any of them. They mocked the two of us together. I was drenched all over with blood, flowing from the god's side, after he had released his spirit. Many cruel fates I endured on that hill. I saw the God of warrior-hosts severely stretched out. A shadowy darkness covered Shield-breaker's corpse with clouds, its shining radiance; a darkness crept over it, black under the sky. All creation wept, lamented the fall of the king. Woden on the tree.

And then, from afar came the elven ones to the god. I beheld it all. I was filled with deep sorrow, yet I bent down to the hands of those creatures, humbly and with great zeal. Then they took the All-father and lifted him from that terrible torment. Those elf-warriors then left me, standing, sprinkled with moisture, punctured all over with tiny arrows. They lay the exhausted god down there and stood by his body’s head, watching over Valholl's Ruler. And he rested there a while, weary after that great battle.

And then, before me his slayer, those brave warriors began to build an earth mound, carved out of the brightest of stone, and placed into it the Lord of Victories. When they had done this, they began to sing a dirge, mournful in the evening hour. Freyr's elves then smeared the mound with blood of horses. They then wearily took their leave of the mighty cosmic one, he rested alone. But we, standing there fixed, wept a good while until the voices of the warriors had faded away. The corpse cooled, fair dwelling of the soul.

And then a man felled us all to the ground. That was a dreadful fate! One of them buried us in a deep pit. However, the Nailed God's thegns, friends, sought me out and adorned me with gold and silver. Now you might have heard, my beloved hero, of that which I have suffered at the hands of evil doers, painful and grievous this was. But now is the time that I should be revered throughout the world and all men from far and wide should chant to this beacon.

On me did the etin's son suffer for a time. For this, I now tower in glory under the heavens and can heal all those who hold me in awe. In olden days I was made the harshest of punishments, hateful to people, before I showed them, the speech bearers, the true path to life. Behold, the God of Spears, Aesir chieftein, honoured me over the forest trees, just as he also honoured his mother, Bestla herself, for all men, over all womankind. Now I call on you my beloved warriors that you speak of this vision to all mankind, reveal with words that it is the tree of glory on which Great Wolf-lord suffered for the conquest of the runes and the mysteries since before Ymir and Ginungagap. Death he tasted there, but the warrior-king rose again with his mighty power to help all mankind. Then he fell screaming, he took the runes upon himself. And he will come again to this middle earth to seek out mankind on Ragnarok, the Spear-God himself, Woden, and his Einherjar with him, that he will then judge everyone according to their deeds and their scars.
Nor should anyone be unafraid of the words the ruler will speak. He will ask before the multitudes where is the person willing to taste bitter death for the sake of his honor's name, as he did beforehand on that tree. But they will be afraid and not know what to say to Woden. But there will be no need to be afraid for any of those who bear before them in their hearts the best of signs. But through the Irminsul shall every soul who desires to dwell in the upper heavens among gods and ancestors.

I prayed to the tree with a joyful heart, with great zeal, there where I was alone with little company. My spirit was inspired with longing to seek the path to the next world, that for which it has yearned for so long. It is now my life’s joy that I might seek the victory tree alone more often than others to honour it well. This desire is strong in my soul and my hope of protection is directed to that pillar.

I don’t have many powerful friends on this earth, for they have passed on from the joys of this world, sought for themselves the king of gods and are living now in the havens with the High Father, dwelling in glory. And I myself long for that day when the arising Irminsul, which I beheld here on earth, will take me from this transitory life and bring me to where there is great bliss, joy in haven, where the sons of Mannaz are seated at the feast, where there is perpetual bliss, and then place me where I can for evermore dwell in glory with the holy ones in bliss.
May Woden be a friend to me, he who suffered that time on the gallows-tree from which no mortal knows where the roots doth grow. He enlightened us and gave us life, the power of the runes. Hope was restored with glory and with joy those who had suffered burning there. The warrior was victorious in that journey, mighty and swift, when he came with the hoards, the company of souls, into Valholl, the Lord of Sword Storms, to the joy of valkyries and all the blessed gods who dwelt in Asgard before, who dwelt in glory, when their chieftein came, Woden, there his homeland was.
